{{Top}} {{Conjecture}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:Shuttle2743Copilot-TMH.png]] |name=Unidentified Imperial shuttle co-pilot |homeworld= |birth= |death=[[9 ABY]], [[Shuttle 2743]]The events of "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]," including the [[death]] of the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[shuttle]] co-[[pilot]] aboard [[Shuttle 2743]], took place in [[9 ABY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. |species=[[Human]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=new |height= |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Brown]] |skin=Light |cyber= |families=new |parents=new |partners=new |siblings=new |children=new |affiliation=*[[Galactic Empire]] *[[Gideon's Imperial remnant]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Destroying your planet was a small price to pay to rid the galaxy of terrorism.|The co-pilot, to Cara Dune|}} A [[human]] [[Gender|male]] '''co-pilot''' served in the [[Galactic Empire]], being aboard the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]] when it [[Destruction of Alderaan|destroyed]] the [[planet]] [[Alderaan]] in [[1 BBY]]. After the Empire was fractured into remnants, he operated with a [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|remnant]] led by [[Moff]] [[Gideon]]. Around [[9 ABY]], he and the primary [[Unidentified Imperial shuttle pilot|pilot]] aboard the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[Operating number|designated]] [[Shuttle 2743]] were pursued by the [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray''-31-class patrol and attack craft]] ''[[Slave I]]'' while ferrying [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]]. The ''Slave I'' immobilized the shuttle and clamped to it, the [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]] entering the [[Starship|vessel]]. The co-[[pilot]] held Pershing at gunpoint, and shot the other pilot when he attempted to resolve the confrontation. He then taunted the Alderaan survivor [[marshal]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] until she shot him. ==Biography== ===Fall of the Empire=== {{Quote|I saw your planet destroyed. I was on the Death Star.''"
"''Which one?''"
"[Laughs]''You think you're funny? Do you know how many millions were killed on those bases?|The co-pilot and Cara Dune, on Alderaan's destruction and the Death Star superweapons|}} During the [[Imperial Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], the Imperial [[pilot]] served on the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|DS-1 Death Star Mobile Battle Station]]. [[Gender|He]] stood witness as the Death Star [[Destruction of Alderaan|destroyed]] the [[planet]] [[Alderaan]] in [[1 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' The Death Star was soon [[Battle of Yavin|destroyed]] by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]]{{Film|IV}} that same [[Standard year|year]], and its successor, the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station]], met a similar [[Battle of Endor|fate]]{{Film|VI}} in [[4 ABY]]. The Empire then fractured into remnants,[[Alphabet Squadron (novel)|''Alphabet Squadron'']] and the co-pilot served in one led by the Imperial [[Moff]] [[Gideon]] by [[9 ABY]], during the [[New Republic Era|reign]] of the [[New Republic]], the Alliance's successor. ===Last stand=== {{Quote|Drop your weapon.''"
"''No. No, you listen to me. This is a top-tier target of the New Republic. This is a clone engineer. And if they find out that he's dead because of you, you're gonna wish you never left Alderaan.|Cara Dune and the co-pilot|}} That [[Standard year|year]], the Imperial was the co-pilot of the [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] [[Operating number|designated]] [[Shuttle 2743]]—serving alongside another [[Unidentified Imperial shuttle pilot|pilot]]—that was tasked with [[Transport|ferrying]] the Imperial scientist and [[Cloning|clone]] [[engineer]] [[Doctor]] [[Penn Pershing]] to [[Gideon's light cruiser]]. However, they were hunted by the [[Firespray-31-class patrol and attack craft|''Firespray''-31-class patrol and attack craft]] ''[[Slave I]]'', which chased the [[shuttle]] through [[Realspace|space]]. Despite the two pilots taking evasive maneuvers, the Firespray kept closing in on them.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} {{AD|Disney+}} Pershing asked what was going on, but the co-pilot told him to be quiet. As the pilots continued trying to outmaneuver the ''Slave I'', the attack craft soon immobilized Shuttle 2743 with an [[Ion cannon]] shot. The pair recalled their hands from the control console to avoid being electricuted by the sudden power surge. The other pilot assessed the losses from the shuttle's systems, and the ''Slave I''{{'s}} pilot, [[Boba Fett]], ordered for Shuttle 2743's [[Deflector shield|shields]] and [[transponder]]s to be disabled, warning of a boarding party. [[File:Pershing-captive-CH16.png|thumb|left|300px|The co-pilot held Pershing at gunpoint much to the other pilot's disagreement.]] Pershing assumed the attackers were [[pirate]]s and asked if they should fight, a request the co-pilot shut down as he complied with Fett's demands, retracting the shuttle's wings in order to link with the ''Slave I''.[[The Mandalorian Season 2 Junior Novel|''The Mandalorian Season 2'' Junior Novel]] The Firespray then passed above Shuttle 2743's cockpit and clamped to the shuttle. The [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]] entered the cockpit shortly after, [[The Mandalorian's IB-94 blaster pistol|blaster]] drawn, and co-pilot and his comrades got out of their seats, the other two raising their hands. The shuttle co-pilot introduced Pershing to Djarin, who had already met the doctor. As the Mandalorian exchanged with Pershing after, the co-pilot held his [[SE-14r light repeating blaster]] to Pershing's head. The New Republic [[marshal]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]] joined Djarin, and the co-pilot told her to stay back, glaring at her. The other pilot attempted to resolve the confrontation, claiming he was not supporting his comrade, but the shuttle co-pilot promptly shot him, [[Death|killing]] the his comrade and scanning the room with his [[eye]]s. Dune asked the co-pilot to drop his weapon, but the Imperial denied her and summarized the importance of Pershing being alive. He also noticed a tear tattoo on the marshal, identifying her as an [[Alderaanian]] and taunting her about her [[homeworld]]'s destruction. When he condemned the deaths of millions aboard both Death Stars, Dune asked him again to drop his [[blaster]], but he continued, calling the riddance of Alderaan a small price to pay against "terrorism." The marshal thus shot him in the face, and she and her associates used the shuttle to [[Second rescue of Grogu|infiltrate]] Gideon's [[Class 546 Cruiser|cruiser]]. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|They're pirates. Shouldn't we fight?''"
"''I don't have a death wish. Do you?|Pershing and the co-pilot|}} [[File:ShutUpPershing-CH16.png|thumb|right|300px|The co-pilot shut down Pershing's questions.]] The Imperial shuttle co-pilot was a [[human]] male with light skin and [[Color|brown]] eyes. He was loyal to the Empire, deeming the destruction of Alderaan and its entire population as justified in ridding the galaxy of "terrorism" but holding the destruction of both Death Stars as unforgivable war crimes. The co-pilot silenced Pershing when the doctor asked of the situation while Shuttle 2743 was pursued. When the doctor suggested fighting the attackers, the co-pilot remarked that he did not have a death wish. Upon Djarin's arrival, the co-pilot was the only Imperial aboard the shuttle to not raise his hands and instead used Pershing as a bargaining chip, stressing the value of the doctor. His refusal to comply to the boarding party drove him to murder his fellow pilot when the man tried to bargain with the intruders. The co-pilot identified Cara Dune as a rebel dropper and also as a Alderaanian from her tear drop tattoo, smiling as he pointed it out. He chose to taunt her about her destroyed homeworld despite her warnings, laughing mockingly when she asked which Death Star he was on. The Imperial's persistence ultimately led to his death. ==Equipment== {{Quote|Drop your blaster.|Cara Dune, to the co-pilot|}} The co-pilot [[Clothing|donned]] a black [[flight suit]] with the [[Imperial crest]] on his shoulders. He also wore an aviator hat with a built in [[comlink]] and black [[glove]]s. The co-pilot wielded an SE-14r light [[repeating blaster]], which he used to hold Pershing at gunpoint. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I'm a jerk in outer space again!!|Thomas E. Sullivan|{{Instagram|username=thomasesullivan_|url=p/CI8h96QlNs7|name=[[Thomas E. Sullivan]]|quote=I'm a jerk in outer space again!!|nobackup=1}}}} The Imperial shuttle co-pilot appeared in "[[Chapter 16: The Rescue]]" of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] [[Disney+]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Peyton Reed]] and released on [[December 18]], [[2020]].{{D23|url=everything-new-you-can-stream-on-disney-in-december-2020|text=Everything New You Can Stream on Disney+ in December 2020}} Credited as "Co-Pilot," he was played by [[Thomas E.
